axes.subFinding: the class predicate selects 36/36: every instance of the domain is 7-2 - the class is the domain. gsl3.statement: GSL-3 (BL-068, the governs semantic layer's first explanatory entry). The fa/ti asymmetry's mechanism is predicate-axis divergence at the contact-target tiers. The fa-pole selects within a two-class governed domain: the A1 tier carries 14 x 7-27 (observed) + 14 x 7-31 (unobserved), the domain is office-flat (28/28), and the intrinsic set-class predicate separates it 14/0/0/14. The ti-pole's contact relation is exhaustive over a single-class tier: the D6 tier carries 14 x 7-2 only, the class predicate restates over the availability domain (36/36), and the sole clean separator is the office-linking condition (14/0/0/22), whose complement is modal-bounded (every unrecorded instance lies at office delta +/-2 mod 7, 11+11). The boundary invariants are pole-universal (both poles: inversion pairs in-class, office sums 6 mod 7, status shared within pairs); the Z-interface polarization is fa-specific (D4 separation 14/14 vs 14/14; D7 mixed at 4/14 Z-majority, non-separating). The class asymmetry (7-27 vs 7-2) is input-level; the selection asymmetry is axis-level (class vs office), and the axis difference is forced by the target tiers' class multiplicity. Same invariants, different predicates.

synthesis.premiseCarried: OD-68-0/OD-68-1: the discrimination domain moves from the collapsed analogue-R (U = O = 14 by construction) to the anchors' recorded relations (14/14/0) and the constructed availability domain (36/14/22); the interpretation of the recollected 'no selection gap' is that the analogue's construction consumed the domain, and the deeper ledger fact is that the recorded layer collapses too while the availability layer does not - the tier's class uniformity is the structural cause.
